propositions: The autouse _no_repo_commits guard invokes git rev-parse HEAD before and after every test, causing ~207 runner-seconds overhead across the full 13,255-test suite (~75s projected macOS wall-time savings).
The current per-test contract requires detecting HEAD movement, naming the responsible test, and preserving allow_repo_writes escape and session dirty-tree backstop without weakening isolation.

Eliminating per-test Git subprocesses requires in-process HEAD fingerprinting via one-time per-worker worktree discovery, but candidate implementations (Dulwich/pygit2/GitPython library adoption or hand-parsing ref storage formats) lack sufficient OSS consensus or meet fidelity constraints.

OSS survey (pytest, pip, poetry, pre-commit) shows 4/4 projects keep source-checkout VCS subprocess work out of per-test hot path, supporting the optimization direction but not endorsing a specific implementation without production code changes.
